Gulf of Alaska walleye pollock data for the Rceattle case study

Source: R/data_documentation.R
sgl_rg_goa_pollock_data.Rd

Inputs for the two models proposed for the 2026 Gulf of Alaska walleye pollock assessment (models 26a and 26b), 1970 to 2026 at ages 1 to 10 with a plus group: catch and age compositions from one fishery, indices and age compositions from four surveys, the covariate Shelikof Strait catchability is measured through and the ten ecosystem series of model 26b, with the estimates Rceattle returns for the same inputs, used to check the bridge.

Usage

sgl_rg_goa_pollock_data

Format

A list with components inputs (dimensions, weight, maturity and natural mortality at age, the ageing error matrix and the two with young ages pooled, the catch, index and composition observations with their use flags and sample sizes, survey and spawn timing, the composition constant, Qcov, the covariates data frame, the bottom trawl catchability prior and the ages Rceattle rescales each selectivity curve at), and m26a and m26b (Rceattle's spawning biomass, recruitment, mean recruitment and its deviations, annual log F, selectivity parameters and the annual offsets of the fishery curve, log catchability and its annual offsets, the Shelikof catchability effect, standard deviation and correlation with the latent series Qcov measures (qcov_latent), the Dirichlet-multinomial parameters, predicted indices, marginal negative log likelihood and number of fixed effects; m26b adds the dsem coefficients by arrow name, the covariate means and the covariate cells). Composition sample sizes and Dirichlet-multinomial parameters are scaled by one plus the number of fitted bins times the composition constant, which is how Rceattle counts them; every other estimate is in Rceattle's own terms.

Source

Monnahan, C., Adams, G., Lauffenberger, N. 2026. Gulf of Alaska pollock model updates. Alaska Fisheries Science Center, September 2026. Inputs from https://github.com/grantdadams/Rceattle-models, fit with Rceattle 5.23.0 (Adams, G. D., Holsman, K. K., Barbeaux, S. J., Dorn, M. W., Ianelli, J. N., Spies, I., Stewart, I. J., Punt, A. E. 2022. An ensemble approach to understand predation mortality for groundfish in the Gulf of Alaska. Fisheries Research 251: 106303).
